name: engine
what: The valuation engine's statement inputs, read from the income statement and balance sheet alone, with depreciation and amortization (D&A) as a memo read from the cash flow statement. Section 3 holds derived figures: G&A, other income excluding interest expense, EBIT, and pretax income including equity-method income. EBITDA is not computed by the template (a memo row is never a term). Cost of revenue takes the direct costs of what the company sells under captions of their own; a right-of-use asset printed beside operating-lease liabilities is an operating-lease asset. Statement checks: only total liabilities and equity, operating income and net income against the company's own printed figures, assets equal to liabilities plus equity as spread, and cash, total assets and revenue against the filed figures decide a statement's outcome; the other sections' subtotal checks are shown and decide nothing. The D&A memo row takes every D&A add-back the cash flow statement prints, each at its printed amount, summed.

rows.name: Cost of revenue
rows.definition: The cost of the goods and services sold, as printed: cost of sales, cost of revenues, cost of goods sold, with the depreciation and amortization the line includes. A company may print that cost as several lines under captions of its own, without the words "cost of revenue": every line that is a direct cost of delivering what the company sells belongs here, whatever its caption and whether or not it is printed on its own line.
belongs: cost of sales, cost of revenues, cost of goods and services sold
content, product, service and subscription costs printed as cost of revenue

the direct costs of delivering the service sold, printed as separate lines under their own captions: the costs of operating the assets that deliver it (crew, fuel, repairs, maintenance, supplies, insurance of those assets), the hire of third-party capacity used to deliver it, and fees for managing those assets day to day

rows.name: Depreciation and amortization (memo, from the cash flow statement)
rows.definition: Memo: the depreciation and amortization add-backs printed in the operating section of the cash flow statement, for the income statement's EBITDA, each at its printed amount. When the statement prints them as one line, that line; when it prints them as separate lines (for example depreciation, and the amortization of intangible assets), each of those lines, and the row is their sum. Every other operating line takes no row here and stays outside the spread.

report_checks.name: total assets against total liabilities and capital, as spread
report_checks.note: Both sides are totals of the spread's rows.

report_checks.name: total assets against total liabilities and equity, as filed
report_checks.note: Checks the filing, not the spread.

report_checks.name: cash and equivalents row against the filed cash and cash equivalents
report_checks.note: When the filing has no cash-and-equivalents total, its cash total (Cash) is read; unavailable when neither is printed. A difference can be restricted cash printed with cash.

report_checks.name: equity rows including noncontrolling interest against the filed total equity
report_checks.note: When the filing has no total equity including noncontrolling interest, its stockholders' equity (StockholdersEquity) is read: the same total when there is no noncontrolling interest, and a difference equal to it otherwise. Unavailable when neither is printed.

report_checks.name: total assets row against the filed total assets
report_checks.note: The assets the rows add up to against the total assets the company printed; unavailable when it prints none.

report_checks.name: revenue row against the filed revenue
report_checks.note: When the filing has no Revenues total, its revenue from contracts with customers is read; unavailable when the company prints no revenue total (a company with no revenue).
